note.explanation: A free-body diagram shows the forces acting on one object. It uses arrows to show the direction and relative magnitude of each force, and labels to name each force.
examples: A book pushed to the right across a table has an applied force to the right and friction to the left.
The table exerts a normal force upward on the book, while the book's weight acts downward.
note.checkAnswer: The book has an applied force to the right, friction to the left, a normal force upward, and weight downward.
note.simple: Draw the object as a box. Add an arrow for every force acting on it, point each arrow in the force's direction, and label it.
note.checkQuestion: A book is pushed to the right across a table. Name the four forces shown in its free-body diagram and give their directions.
note.title: Drawing a Free-Body Diagram
steps: Represent the object by a box.
Draw each force arrow outward from the centre of the box.
Point each arrow in the direction of the force.
Use arrow length to show the force's relative magnitude.
Label each arrow with the exact type of force.
note.answer: A free-body diagram is used to show the relative magnitudes and directions of all the forces acting on an object in a given situation.

options: A picture of the whole room
mcqs.stem: In a free-body diagram, how is the object usually represented?
rationales: This is correct: the textbook says the object is usually represented by a box.
This is wrong because the diagram focuses on forces acting on the object, not the whole room.
This is wrong because a curved path does not represent the object in the diagram.
This is wrong because a list of masses alone does not show the forces or their directions.

options: Outward from the centre of the box
mcqs.stem: Where are force arrows usually drawn in a free-body diagram?
rationales: This is wrong because the textbook's method draws arrows outward from the centre.
This is correct: the force arrows are drawn outward from the centre of the box.
This is wrong because arrows along the outline do not clearly show forces acting on the object.
This is wrong because the textbook shows the arrows starting at the centre of the represented object.

mcqs.stem: In a free-body diagram, what reflects the magnitude of a force?
rationales: This is wrong because the arrowhead indicates the direction of the force.
This is wrong because the label tells the type of force, not its magnitude.
This is correct: the length of a force arrow reflects the force's magnitude.
This is wrong because the box represents the object and its size is not the force magnitude.

mcqs.stem: Which part of a force arrow indicates the direction in which the force acts?
rationales: This is correct: the arrowhead indicates the direction of the force.
This is wrong because arrow length reflects magnitude, not direction.
This is wrong because the box's position does not show the direction of a force.
This is wrong because the label names the force; its first letter does not indicate direction.

mcqs.stem: What should a force label indicate in a free-body diagram?
rationales: This is correct: each force is labelled to indicate its exact type.
This is wrong because the label is for the force, not just the object's name.
This is wrong because the force label does not state the object's speed.
This is wrong because the force label does not state how long the force acts.

mcqs.stem: In the textbook's diagram of a book pushed to the right across a table, which way do the applied force and friction point?
rationales: This is correct: the diagram shows applied force right and friction left.
This is wrong because it reverses the directions shown in the textbook's diagram.
This is wrong because the applied force and friction are shown horizontally, not upward.
This is wrong because the applied force and friction are shown horizontally, not downward.

mcqs.stem: In the textbook's free-body diagram of a book on a table, which force arrow points downward?
rationales: This is wrong because the normal force arrow points upward in the diagram.
This is correct: the weight arrow points downward.
This is wrong because the applied force arrow points horizontally to the right.
This is wrong because the friction arrow points horizontally to the left.

options: They show relative magnitudes and directions of forces acting on an object.
They show only the object's path.
They show only forces that do not touch the object.
mcqs.stem: What is the main purpose of a free-body diagram?
rationales: This is correct: a free-body diagram shows the relative magnitudes and directions of forces acting on an object.
This is wrong because a path alone does not represent the forces on the object.
This is wrong because the diagram shows all forces acting on the object, not only non-contact forces.
This is wrong because the diagram represents forces, not the object's dimensions.

written.text: Describe the motion of a block on a table taking into account the friction between the two surfaces. What is the static friction and kinetic friction?
written.finalAnswer: Static friction acts between surfaces at rest relative to each other; kinetic friction acts when the surfaces slide relative to each other. Friction opposes relative motion or its tendency.

example.question: Suppose a book is pushed over the surface of a table top as shown in Fig.3.8(a). Then how can we represent the forces acting on the body using free-body diagram?
example.answer: Represent the book by a box. Draw and label arrows outward from its centre: normal force upward, weight downward, friction to the left, and applied force to the right. The arrow lengths reflect relative magnitudes.

explain.title: What a free-body diagram shows
explain.body: “Free-body diagrams are used to show the relative magnitudes and directions of all the forces acting on an object in a given situation.” In other words, a free-body diagram is a special example of the vector diagrams.

explain.title: How to draw the forces
explain.body: Usually, the object is represented by a box and the force arrows are drawn outward from the centre of the box in the directions of forces. The length of a force arrow reflects the magnitude of the force and the arrow head indicates the direction in which the force acts. Each force is labelled to indicate the exact type of force.

explain.title: Forces shown on a book
explain.body: For a book pushed to the right across a table, the textbook's diagram shows the applied force to the right, friction to the left, normal force upward, and weight downward.

mistakes: Leaving out a force acting on the object, such as weight or the table's normal force.
Pointing an arrow in the wrong direction or drawing its arrowhead unclearly.
Starting arrows from the edge of the box instead of outward from its centre.
Using arrow length to show direction; direction is shown by the arrowhead, while length reflects magnitude.
Forgetting to label each force with its exact type.
